title_guess: GDP vs GNP vs NDP vs NNP as a two-round contest: which one is national income, and which one compares countries' growth
recurring_cast: four bodybuilder contestants labelled GDP, GNP, NDP, NNP (photo-real cutouts; each has its own pose)
stage_with_spotlight (truss frame with stage lights, a green beam and a name plate on the stage front)
round_number_card held up by two hands (Round 1 at bottom left, Round 2 at right)
definition card in an olive box beside the stage, with a short capitalised heading added later (INTERNAL STRENGTH, EFFICIENCY ...)
title_sash and big 'NI' letters on the NNP contestant
podium_steps 1-2-3 at bottom left; the step of the current reason rises
header card 'why GNP is not used' with a small GNP contestant struck by a red cross
formula line GNP = GDP + NFIA, whose parts change colour and get arrows
running_examples: dual citizen of Country X and Country Y works in Country Z and produces goods worth Rs 100; both X and Y count the Rs 100 in their GNP
GNP = GDP + NFIA with GDP falling (jobs falling) while NFIA rises fast, so GNP still rises

best_moments.why: the four measures in a tree turn into four contestants in a line-up and a 'Round 1' card is raised: a dry list becomes a contest with a judge's question (most accurate national income?)
the winner of round 1 gets a title sash and big 'NI' letters beside him: 'NNP at factor cost is given the title of national income' is shown literally as a title
camera pulls back to all four contestants on one stage, only NNP wearing the sash: the other three are still measures of national income, but only one holds the title
a rule card ('measures using depreciation not allowed') puts red crosses on NDP and NNP, they leave, and a 'VS' drops between GDP and GNP: elimination by a rule, visible

a person doing the splits across two country boxes = dual citizen; he then stands on Country Z with 'Rs 100' and two curved arrows from X and Y both land on the same Rs 100: double counting as two claims on one coin

in the formula GNP = GDP + NFIA the GDP part turns red with a down-arrow to a red JOBS box, the NFIA part turns green with a tall up-arrow, and GNP gets a green up-arrow: a misleading total shown on its own parts
a three-step podium at the corner counts the reasons; the step for the current reason rises (cheap, clear 'reason 1 of 3' device)

weak_moments.why: each contestant's turn (about 20-50 s) is a paragraph definition card next to a posing figure; the pose shows 'strength' but nothing shows the border (GDP), residents abroad (GNP) or wear and tear (NDP/NNP)
the opening tree already puts a green tick on NNP before the contest is announced, so the round 1 result is given away
the NDP card says NDP shows achievements in R&D because it considers depreciation; the formula GDP minus depreciation is spoken but never written; the R&D link is doubtful and should be checked
per capita income is a text fraction (NNP at factor cost over total population) with no picture of the population sharing the income; the lead-in words at 175-180 s are missing from the transcript
the dual-citizenship double counting claim is doubtful (national accounts assign each person to one resident economy, not by citizenship); describe it, do not reuse it unchecked
on-screen wording drifts: the GNP card says 'residents and businesses', the NNP card says 'citizens overseas and domestically'; the two bases are not the same
photo-real bodybuilder cutouts; BIE will not use photos and should draw its own generic contestant figures

segments.teaches: this video is a contest between GDP, GNP, NDP and NNP; the winner of round 1 is the one that gives the most accurate value of national income

elements.what: 'National Income' heading chip
four branches from the chip to GDP, GNP, NDP, NNP on a green strip
green tick beside NNP
four bodybuilder cutouts in a row, each labelled with one measure
'ROUND 1' card raised from the bottom edge by two hands

segments.notes: 4 change events. The tree moves to a small chip at top left and the four labels become four contestants as 'competition' is said. The NNP tick appears before the contest starts (spoiler).
segments.idea: the four measures will compete; round 1 asks which gives the truest national income
segments.shown_as: a 'National Income' chip draws four branches down to GDP, GNP, NDP and NNP and a green tick lands on NNP; then the chip moves to the corner, the four labels become four bodybuilders standing in a line, and two hands raise a 'Round 1' card from the bottom edge

segments.teaches: GDP is the money value of all goods and services produced inside a country's geographical boundary; it shows the economy's internal strength and whether jobs are being created

elements.what: stage: truss frame with lights, a green spotlight beam and a name plate 'GDP'
GDP bodybuilder posing alone in the beam
'Round 1' card held at bottom left
definition card at right, 'geographical boundary' in green
'INTERNAL STRENGTH' heading added on top of the card
short line down from the card to 'JOB CREATION'

segments.notes: 3 change events in 22 s. The stage turns grey and stays for all of round 1; only the contestant, plate and card change. The figure's muscles are a metaphor for 'strength'; the border idea itself is only in the text.
segments.idea: GDP counts what is produced inside the border, so it shows the economy's own (internal) strength and job creation
segments.shown_as: the canvas clears to a grey stage under a truss of lights; the GDP contestant poses alone in a green spotlight over his name plate; a definition card writes on beside the stage with 'geographical boundary' in green, an 'INTERNAL STRENGTH' heading is added on top, and a short line drops from the card to 'JOB CREATION'

segments.teaches: GNP is the money value of goods and services produced by a country's residents (and businesses), wherever they are; it shows internal and external strength, i.e. how much the world depends on the country and the country on the world

elements.what: GDP contestant replaced by the GNP contestant in a new pose; name plate now 'GNP'
new definition card: residents and businesses, not restricted by the boundary
'INTERNAL & EXTERNAL STRENGTH' heading
note under the card on a line: how much the outside world depends on its product and how much it depends on the world
next two figures slide in from the left as the turn ends

segments.notes: 5 change events in 47 s (~every 9 s, but 45-73 s has no change). Transcript gap 54.2-61.4 s (the 'not only in India but abroad too' part). Card says 'residents', the NNP card later says 'citizens'.
segments.idea: GNP counts what the country's residents produce anywhere, so it also shows the country's ties with the outside world
segments.shown_as: the GDP contestant is swapped for the GNP contestant in a new pose and the plate changes to GNP; a new definition card writes on ('not restricted by the geographical boundary'), an 'INTERNAL & EXTERNAL STRENGTH' heading is added, and a line drops to a note about the world depending on the country and the country on the world; at the end the next figures slide in from the left

segments.teaches: NDP is GDP minus depreciation; the video says depreciation can only be cut if R&D improves, so NDP over time shows whether the economy's efficiency is rising or falling

elements.what: NDP contestant in a twisting floor pose; plate 'NDP'
card: shows achievements in R&D because it considers depreciation ('R&D' in green)
'EFFICIENCY' heading

segments.notes: 3 change events in 27 s. The formula GDP minus depreciation is spoken (91-96 s) but never written. The R&D-depreciation link is doubtful; flag before reuse.
segments.idea: NDP removes wear and tear of capital from GDP and is read as a sign of efficiency
segments.shown_as: the NDP contestant takes the stage in a twisting floor pose over a new plate; a short card writes on beside him linking NDP to R&D and depreciation, and an 'EFFICIENCY' heading is added on top; nothing on screen shows depreciation being subtracted

segments.teaches: NNP is GNP minus depreciation; since it counts only the country's own residents' production and removes depreciation it is the purest form of national income; NNP at factor cost is titled national income and written NI

elements.what: NNP contestant standing square to the camera; plate 'NNP'
card: value of finished goods and services by a country's citizens overseas and at home, 'minus depreciation' in green
'PUREST FORM OF THE INCOME OF A NATION' heading
'@ factor Cost' added to the NNP name plate
diagonal title sash on the NNP contestant
big serif 'NI' letters beside the contestant

segments.notes: 6 change events in 50 s; 117-152 s has no change while the GNP-minus-depreciation idea is repeated in speech. 'Factor cost' is added to the plate without being explained in this video.
segments.idea: NNP at factor cost is the purest measure and carries the title 'national income' (NI)
segments.shown_as: the NNP contestant takes the stage; his card writes on with 'minus depreciation' in green and later gets a 'purest form of the income of a nation' heading; then '@ factor cost' is added to his name plate, a title sash appears across his chest and big 'NI' letters pop up beside him, like a champion getting his title

segments.teaches: GDP, GNP and NDP also measure national income, but if one of them must be called national income it is NNP

elements.what: all four contestants together on the wide stage, NNP at the end wearing the sash, plate 'NNP @ factor cost' above him
'Round 1' card still at bottom left

segments.notes: 2 big change events: zoom out (163-169 s), zoom back in to NNP alone with NI (174-175 s) as NNP is named.
segments.idea: all four are ways to measure national income; only NNP at factor cost holds the title
segments.shown_as: the camera pulls back from NNP to show all four contestants posing side by side on the stage, only NNP wearing the title sash and the 'factor cost' tag; as the narrator says 'it will be NNP' the camera pushes back in on NNP alone with his NI letters

segments.teaches: per capita income = NNP at factor cost divided by total population (nominal PCI); removing inflation up to the base year gives real PCI, which is the right measure of economic growth

elements.what: line down from the NNP card to 'PER CAPITA INCOME (PCI)'
'Nominal PCI =' NNP at factor cost over total population
white box: real PCI is found by adjusting for inflation
after the card clears: 'REAL PCI' label on a white speech box 'most appropriate measure of economic growth'

segments.notes: 7 change events in 35 s (~every 5 s); the fraction is built piece by piece as spoken. Transcript gap 175.2-179.7 s at the start of this part. No numbers are used.
segments.idea: share national income over the population to get per capita income, then remove inflation to see real growth
segments.shown_as: a line drops from the NNP card to 'per capita income'; a fraction writes on piece by piece (NNP at factor cost over total population) and gets the label 'nominal PCI'; a white box adds that real PCI adjusts for inflation; then the card clears and a white speech box tagged 'REAL PCI' says it is the most appropriate measure of growth

segments.teaches: round 2: which measure can compare economic growth across countries; measures that use depreciation are not allowed because each government sets its own depreciation rates, so NDP and NNP are out and the contest is GDP vs GNP

elements.what: all four contestants on a bigger stage
'Round 2' card raised at right
yellow banner across the truss: which of these can compare growth of different countries
grey rule card: measures that use depreciation are not allowed
white speech box above the rule: depreciation rates are set by each government and vary a lot
red crosses over NDP and NNP
'VS' between GDP and GNP after the other two leave

segments.notes: 9 change events in 57 s; 235-259 s has no change while the rule is repeated. The rule card and its reason (callout) are both text; the elimination itself is pictorial.
segments.idea: for comparing countries, drop every measure that depends on each government's depreciation rules; GDP and GNP remain
segments.shown_as: the stage widens to hold all four contestants and a 'Round 2' card rises at right; a yellow banner with the round's question stretches across the truss; a grey rule card and a speech box above it give the depreciation rule and its reason; red crosses pop over NDP and NNP, the two leave, and GDP and GNP move to opposite sides with a 'VS' between them

segments.teaches: reason 1 against GNP: with dual citizenship, a person who is a citizen of X and Y but works in Z adds Rs 100 of output that both X and Y count in their GNP, so GNP double counts

elements.what: header card: why GNP is not used to compare growth of countries
small GNP contestant with a red cross at the header's left
three-step podium 1-2-3 at bottom left; step 1 raised
black person icon labelled 'dual citizenship'
person doing the splits across blue 'Country X' and 'Country Y' boxes
X and Y slide apart; person stands on a yellow 'Country Z' box with 'Rs 100' under it
two curved arrows labelled GNP from X and from Y meeting at the Rs 100

segments.notes: 9 change events in 47 s (~every 5 s). Running example: Rs 100 output by a dual citizen. The claim itself is doubtful (GNP is based on residence, and each person is resident in one economy); describe, do not certify.
segments.idea: if one person's output is claimed by two countries, adding up GNPs counts it twice
segments.shown_as: on a white canvas under a 'why GNP is not used' header (a crossed-out GNP contestant at its side), a person icon does the splits across two blue boxes, Country X and Country Y; the boxes slide apart and the person stands on a yellow Country Z box with 'Rs 100' under it; 'GNP' labels appear under X and Y and two curved arrows sweep down from both and meet on the same Rs 100
segments.example: dual citizen of X and Y working in Z produces Rs 100; both X and Y count Rs 100 in GNP

segments.teaches: reason 2 against GNP: GNP = GDP + net factor income from abroad, which depends on foreign exchange rates; exchange rates keep fluctuating, so GNP fluctuates and cross-country comparison becomes hard

elements.what: podium step 2 raised
GNP = GDP + Net Factor Income from Abroad (NFIAD), NFIA part in a blue band
line down from NFIA to 'Foreign Exchange Rates'
small two-way arrow and red '[Fluctuates]'
dotted green elbow arrow from 'Fluctuates' back up to GNP

segments.notes: 5 change events in 28 s. The on-screen acronym is NFIAD; spoken 'NFIAD yaani net factor income from abroad'. No numbers.
segments.idea: GNP carries an exchange-rate-driven part, so it wobbles for reasons unrelated to production
segments.shown_as: the dual-citizen picture clears and podium step 2 rises; the formula GNP = GDP + NFIA writes on with the NFIA part in a blue band; a line drops from NFIA to 'foreign exchange rates', a small two-way arrow and a red 'fluctuates' tag appear, and a dotted green arrow loops from 'fluctuates' back up to GNP

segments.teaches: reason 3 against GNP: GDP moves with jobs; if GDP falls (unemployment rises) but NFIA rises fast enough, GNP still grows, giving a misleading picture of growth

elements.what: exchange-rate branch removed; podium step 3 raised
red down-arrow on GDP; GDP part turns pink
line from GDP down to a red 'JOBS' box
tall green up-arrow beside NFIA, NFIA band turns green
green up-arrow on GNP
light blue panel framing the formula
caption under the panel: GNP does not tell if the economy is growing or shrinking

segments.notes: 5 change events in 39 s. Arrows match the spoken directions (GDP down, jobs down, NFIA up, GNP up). 'GDP is directly proportional to jobs' is said as a rule; it is a simplification.
segments.idea: GNP can show growth while the home economy and its jobs are shrinking
segments.shown_as: the exchange-rate branch is wiped and podium step 3 rises; a red down-arrow lands on the GDP part, which turns pink, and a line drops to a red JOBS box; the NFIA part turns green with a tall green up-arrow and a green up-arrow appears on GNP; a blue panel frames the formula and a caption under it says GNP cannot tell growing from shrinking
segments.example: GDP down and jobs down, NFIA up fast, GNP up

segments.teaches: verdict of round 2: GDP, not GNP, is used to compare the economic growth of different countries
